content_html_sanitized:
Posted May 10, 2001
(MarijuanaNews note: During the Clinton years, Republican Drug War hawks claimed that Clinton was abandoning the Drug War, even as arrests soared.
See
NORML Reports: In 1999, A New Record for Marijuana Arrests! 4,175,357 Americans Have Been Arrested During the Clinton Administration.

One of the most absurd and cynical arguments that they used was the claim that " drug use " had gone up because Clinton cut the staff of the Drug Czar’s office. As though that collection of hacks and ideologues had any impact on young people who had never heard of it.

In fact, Bush even repeated this claim during the campaign, long after Clinton’s Czars, first Lee Brown and then McCaffrey, had rebuilt the staff to be larger than ever.

The Drug Czar’s office is essentially about fighting the anti-prohibitionist movement and using " drug education " as prohibitionist propaganda, but Clinton at least left the DEA and the FBI in the hands of professionals.

Now Bush has politicized the Drug War completely. The choice of John Ashcroft as Attorney General seemed to be an aberration, a sop to the far right. However, with the appointment of John Walters as Drug Czar, and Asa Hutchinson as head of the DEA, and the likely nomination of former DEA Director, John Lawn to head the FBI, we now have the complete politicization of all of the agencies.

Hutchinson is the oddest of these appointments. Although he is a former US Attorney, a federal prosecutor, he has no background to suggest any aptitude for the job. His total lack of knowledge about the subject of " drugs " was illustrated by his comments on Politically Incorrect on August 23, 1999, " If you do wave a drug war like they've done in Europe and some of the Scandinavian countries, you go down and you can buy heroin at the convenience store. You can buy marijuana. I just don't think that's the direction that we want to move in our society. And even if you say, " We're gonna solve some problems, " it still doesn't do away with the harm that it does to teenagers and young people. "
See
The Appalling Idiots Who Govern Us

He is going to be running DEAland’s global Drug War and he thinks that you can buy heroin at the 7/11 in Scandinavia, or somewhere!

Even if Hutchinson were not such a boob, it will take a new man some time to get up to speed, and this is likely to demoralize the staff. So why was someone so manifestly incompetent chosen for so important a position? Why was a career DEA officer dumped as the head of the agency?

The answer, I think, is that Hutchinson is, above all, a very reliable partisan Republican. He was on the House prosecutorial team that tried to get the Senate to convict Clinton.

AND, he is from Arkansas, so he knows everything there is to know about the CIA's Mena, Arkansas, guns for cocaine operation that nearly brought down the Reagan/Bush administration and the cover-up that haunted the Clinton Administration.
See the following in the Progressive Review.
BUSH TO NAME MENA DRUG
COVER-UP FIGURE TO HEAD DEA

If Bush wanted a really effective head of the DEA, Hutchinson would be an absurd appointment, which indeed he is. However, if Bush wanted to be sure that the agency that might blow the whistle on the CIA’s involvement in drug smuggling is in friendly hands, Hutchinson is the perfect appointment, so there he is

This is a particularly sensitive time for that very sensitive subject.

As the NORML press release below makes clear, there are many reasons to object to this appointment, but " the good news " is that this is the wrong team at the wrong time for the wrong reasons and it is going to backfire. Certainly, this group is going to even further alienate the Western Europeans who are moving away from DEAland’s leadership in the global Drug War.)

o HUTCHINSON SUPPORTS OVERRIDING FEDERAL LAW TO ALLOW FEDERAL FUNDS TO INFLUENCE STATE ELECTIONS

During Congressional hearings in 1999, Hutchinson criticized government officials for failing to spend federal dollars to persuade voters to reject state initiatives aimed at legalizing medical marijuana and reforming prison sentencing. Upon learning that such behavior would be in violation of federal law (Federal tax dollars may not be used to influence state elections.), Hutchinson proposed Congress override the law so that federal monies could be specifically used to influence voters in states with pending drug reform initiatives. Hutchinson also urged federal officials, including the President and Vice President, " go into those states (with pending initiatives) and say this is bad for the country. "

It's possible that Hutchinson's views on this issue may be at odds with President Bush, who also opposes the medical use of marijuana but backs states' rights to decide the issue. " I believe each state can choose that decision as they choose, " he has said.

For more information on the Hutchinson and Walters' nominations, please contact Keith Stroup, Executive Director of NORML, at (202) 483-5500 or Allen St. Pierre, Executive Director of The NORML Foundation, at (202) 483-8751.
